summary: Iter 12 — Unified Audit Timeline (/api/saas/audit-timeline + /saas-admin UI tab). Backend: 14/15 pytest pass (test_audit_timeline.py). One real backend bug found: naive ISO date in ?since/?until causes 500 due to tz-naive vs tz-aware datetime comparison in audit_timeline_routes._ts_dt. Frontend Playwright: end-to-end PASS — login → audit-timeline-tab → content renders heading 'سجل التدقيق الموحّد', filters card, 31 events; type=impersonation filter narrows to 22; clear restores to 31; tenant_id filter narrows to 28. Regression: capacity card (8/500), tenant-debts (2 rows), MAX_TENANTS=500 all intact. No console errors/warnings, no duplicate-key warnings.

critical.issue: Returns HTTP 500 — TypeError 'can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes' at audit_timeline_routes.py:193 (_ts_dt). Spec example '?since=2026-01-01&?until=2026-12-31' will crash. _parse_iso returns a naive datetime for date-only ISO strings while event timestamps in events list end up tz-aware (the fallback uses datetime.min UTC-aware). Fix: normalize both sides to tz-aware UTC (e.g. `if dt.tzinfo is None: dt = dt.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)`) before the >=/<= comparisons on both _ts_dt(e) result and since_dt/until_dt.

minor.issue: Each wallet-topup event sets admin_email = wallet_transactions.created_by, which is currently the admin email (works for current data) but in many wallet flows created_by may store a user_id rather than an email. Verify the source of truth and consider explicitly resolving admin_id→email for consistency with impersonation/reminder events.

Each source query applies .limit(limit) BEFORE the merge+sort. With limit=200 and one noisy source (e.g., 500 reminders), the merged feed silently loses older events from the other two sources. Consider over-fetching (e.g., 3×limit per source then trim post-sort) or paginating by timestamp.

?admin_id is applied to impersonation (admin_id) and reminders (sent_by_admin_id) but NOT to wallet_topup — that source has no admin field to match on. This is implicit; the spec implies admin filter covers all three. Either document the limitation or store admin_id on admin_deposit wallet transactions.

action_items: HIGH: Fix the tz-naive vs tz-aware datetime crash in /app/backend/routes/saas/audit_timeline_routes.py (_ts_dt + since/until comparison). One-liner: normalize since_dt/until_dt with `dt.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc) if dt and dt.tzinfo is None else dt` and do the same inside _ts_dt before comparing. SPEC date examples '?since=2026-01-01' currently crash.
MINOR: Consider over-fetching per source (3×limit) before merging so a noisy single source doesn't starve others in the merged window.
MINOR: For wallet_topup events, prefer a dedicated admin_id→email lookup rather than relying on wallet_transactions.created_by string field.
critical_code_review_comments: audit_timeline_routes.py:26-32 — _parse_iso silently returns None on any parse error (including a datetime object passed in, since .replace('Z',...) is a str method). Combined with the `or datetime.min.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)` fallback in _ts_dt, this means raw datetime objects from MongoDB collapse to datetime.min for sort/filter purposes. Today the test_events_sorted_desc passes because all DB timestamps are persisted as strings — but the function should defensively handle datetime objects too (isinstance check returning the value as-is, with tz attached).
audit_timeline_routes.py:80,110,145 — `.sort(...).limit(limit).to_list(limit)`: see minor issue above (per-source limit before merge).
audit_timeline_routes.py:35-40 — _to_iso is defined but never used. Dead code, remove.

audit_timeline_routes.py:115 — severity for reminder uses 'warning' when not delivered. That feels backwards relative to impersonation (active=warning). Recommend documenting the severity ladder once: info=success, warning=open/in-progress, critical=failure or sensitive action.

audit_timeline_routes.py:167-170 — Arabic summary is hard-coded; consider extracting Arabic strings to a single i18n dict for easier localization (already mixed with English in some payloads — wallet_transactions.description is shown raw).

SaasAdminPage.js:2078 — `bg-${sevColor}-500` uses dynamic Tailwind class concatenation. Tailwind JIT may purge these classes in production unless 'bg-red-500/bg-amber-500/bg-emerald-500' are present in safelist or explicitly used elsewhere. Recommend a static map: `const dot = {critical:'bg-red-500', warning:'bg-amber-500', info:'bg-emerald-500'}[ev.severity]`.

SaasAdminPage.js (file size) — already 3011 lines. This is a maintainability red flag (>700 LoC rule). Strongly consider splitting each tab into its own component file (AuditTimelineTab.jsx, TenantDebtsTab.jsx, etc.) so state/handlers co-locate with their UI.

rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE: audit_timeline_routes.py:189-195 — `_ts_dt(e)` falls back to `datetime.min.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)` (aware) but `since_dt`/`until_dt` parsed from a date-only ISO string '2026-01-01' via datetime.fromisoformat() are tz-NAIVE. Python raises TypeError on `aware >= naive`. REPRO: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <super_admin_token>' '<BACKEND>/api/saas/audit-timeline?until=2000-01-01'` → 500. Backend log: 'TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes' at line 193. MITIGATION: Add `if since_dt and since_dt.tzinfo is None: since_dt = since_dt.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)` (and same for until_dt) right after `_parse_iso` calls. Additionally fix `_ts_dt` to attach UTC tz to any naive datetime it gets back from _parse_iso. This also makes the function safer if Mongo returns naive datetime objects.
